saints.name: St. Angela Merici
saints.title: Virgin, Founder
saints.shortBlurb: A Franciscan tertiary of Brescia who founded the first teaching order of women to raise up Christian girls…
biography: Born at Desenzano on Lake Garda on 21 March 1474 and orphaned at ten, Angela went with her sister to live at Salò and became a Franciscan tertiary. A vision of her dead sister among the saints, and a later vision of maidens ascending to heaven, fixed her calling to the Christian training of girls.

On pilgrimage to the Holy Land in 1524 she was struck blind at Candia on Crete, yet pressed on and recovered her sight at the same spot on her return. At the jubilee of 1525 Pope Clement VII urged her to remain in Rome, but she withdrew to Brescia and her work.

On 25 November 1535 she bound herself with twelve companions in the Company of St. Ursula, the first order of women dedicated to the education of girls, whose members lived uncloistered in their own homes; within four years they numbered twenty-eight.

Angela died at Brescia on 27 January 1540, leaving twenty-four communities of the Company; from it grew the Order of St. Ursula, whose nuns spread her schools across the world. She was beatified in 1768 and canonized in 1807, and her feast is now kept on the day of her death.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Ursulines for the education of girls.
